title: LESYMAP Installation (macOS)
text:
LESYMAP is a useful package that allows you to conduct Lesion to Symptom Mapping in R.
In the past, other people and I have experienced difficulties when installing this package. In this post, I describe the steps that I followed to install LESYMAP on a Mac operating system (Sequoia 15.5).

Step 1
Install cmake https://cmake.org


Step 2
Add cmake to your path in the R Studio Terminal
touch ~/.zshrc  #creates zshrc file
open -e ~/.zshrc #opens file
export PATH="/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin:$PATH" #adds path
source ~/.zshrc #save
cmake --version #check that cmake is on path


Step 3
Install Gfortran https://github.com/R-macos/gcc-14-branch/releases


Step 4
From the R Studio Console, install the required packages
mylist = c("Rcpp", "RcppArmadillo", "graphics", "grDevices", 
           "magic", "magrittr", "misc3d", "pixmap",
           "psych", "rsvd", "stats", "utils", 
           "lmPerm", "nparcomp" )
needindx =  ! mylist %in% installed.packages()
if (any(needindx)) install.packages(mylist[needindx])


Step 5
Install LESYMAP and dependencies from the Terminal
git clone https://github.com/stnava/ITKR.git
git clone https://github.com/stnava/ANTsRCore.git
git clone https://github.com/stnava/ANTsR.git
git clone https://github.com/dorianps/LESYMAP.git
R CMD INSTALL ITKR
R CMD INSTALL ANTsRCore
R CMD INSTALL ANTsR
R CMD INSTALL LESYMAP


Step 6
Test the installation, as described in the package documentation: https://github.com/dorianps/LESYMAP/wiki/Testing-LESYMAP-installation

title: Research
section: - Neural correlates of communication deficits in post-stroke aphasia
text:
- Neural correlates of communication deficits in post-stroke aphasia
This project focuses on ‘functional communication’, that is the ability to reach a communication goal in a real-world context, in individuals with post-stroke aphasia. Our research examines whether we can predict communication outcomes using information from different brain imaging modalities (e.g., lesion size, lesion location, structural and functional connectivity). This research aims to (1) further our understanding of the mechanisms underlying real-world communication and their neural correlates, and (2) create predictive models which can be used to inform clinical prognosis and treatment strategies.

title: Research
text:
- Narrative comprehension
Using functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI), this project investigates the roles of the semantic network (particularly the Anterior Temporal Lobe) and Default Mode Network in maintaining a situation model of the narrative (i.e., a mental representation of the events, characters and context in the story).
